messages:
Priya M.: FYI ACME procurement just confirmed they will only issue a PO that splits charges across two legal entities. They still want a 12‑month committed plan but will front 8 months by PO. Need deal desk + finance guidance on how to map Marketplace billing (private offer) to split entities. PO attached in thread.

Sam G.: short answer: marketplace private offer can support a single PO tied to a PPO, but split billing across two entities is unusual. We can either: 1) two SKUs + consolidated commitment, or 2) single PPO with internal chargeback. Need Deal Desk approval for any off‑standard credit. @Finance - Raj / @Legal - Tess any red flags? :thinking:

Liam K.: pricing constraints: our marketplace ratecard allows up to 30% off for commits, but margin floor triggers earlier. Proposed commercial: 20% off list + $30k one‑time customer credit to cover initial shortfall while PO ramps. This keeps ASP > margin floor.

Ana R.: procurement constraint: their marketplace team says credits must be visible on invoice or as a separate rebate schedule — they don't accept "silent" internal credits. That affects revenue recognition. Finance needs to confirm acceptable mechanism.

Legal - Tess: for split billing we need a contract amendment that: (a) ties the PPO to the committed quantity, (b) documents allocation across two legal entities, and (c) shows invoice/credit handling. I can draft a short amendment but need whether credit is on‑invoice or off‑invoice.

Billing Bot: Related docs: https://redwood.internal/billing/marketplace-private-offer-mapping (link) and sample mapping CSV: sku,entity,percent

Priya M.: customer timeline: POC starts next Mon. They need a POC PO this week, then convert to marketplace private offer on month 2. Can we offer a POC PO that later converts without losing pricing/commit credits?

Sam G.: we can: define POC as a convertible PO that syndicates into the PPO subject to Deal Desk approval. Two action items for approval: 1) approve 20% list discount + $30k credit (credit treatment TBD) 2) allow convertible PO path that maps to PPO on conversion.

Liam K.: proposed commit/sku snippet:
```
Commit: 12-mo (convertible) / 500k tokens/mo
List price: $0.001/token
Offered price: $0.0008/token (20% off)
One-time credit: $30,000 (to be applied as invoice credit or rebate)
Marketplace SKUs:
- sku.redwood.dedicated.500k
- sku.redwood.dedicated.burst
```

Finance - Raj: If credit is on-invoice we need AR treatment; if rebate we have to run a manual rebate schedule and hit MRR/ARR modeling. On-invoice credit is simpler operationally but procurement may reject it. I'll confirm by EOD.

Legal - Tess: I'll draft amendment language for both credit flows (on-invoice vs rebate). Also need a clause stating conversion terms for the POC PO to PPO to avoid double-billing.

Priya M.: Customer ask: can we allow split-invoice so each legal entity receives separate invoice lines (50/50)? They prefer that for their internal approvals.

Sam G.: Operationally we can map % allocation per SKU in the PPO mapping CSV. This is off-standard but doable with one-time manual setup. We need Deal Desk approval to accept split-invoice mapping for this account and to approve the 20% + $30k credit.

Liam K.: tagging the margin team: this deal reduces unit price below our typical ratecard. Approve only if Deal Desk confirms the credit is capped and non-recurring.

Priya M.: Requesting Deal Desk approval: 20% discount + $30k one-time credit + allow split-invoice mapping for Marketplace private offer; convertible POC PO allowed. Please respond by 5pm PST so we can start POC next week. :pray:

Sam G.: @DealDesk please review — adding summary + required finance checkbox.

Billing Bot: Automated note: if approved, run SKU allocation CSV upload to billing system before PPO activation.

Finance - Raj: noted, will confirm by 4pm.

Legal - Tess: I'll circulate draft amendment by EOD for signoff.

Priya M.: thanks — will keep customer updated.

(React: ✅ from Sam G., :thumbsup: from Liam K.)
